titlePlain: Why You Can't Apply Classical Practices

steps.label: 1. Measurement is inherently probabilistic
steps.sub: Same correct circuit, different raw counts on every run

steps.label: 2. Real hardware is noisy, and it drifts
steps.sub: Gate errors and decoherence change between calibration cycles

steps.label: 3. The SDK ecosystem is unusually unstable
steps.sub: Qiskit's 0.x to 1.0 transition removed and renamed core APIs

eyebrow: Mapping classical practice onto quantum code
code:
Unit tests, exact assertions
  -> construction tests stay exact;
     measurement tests become statistical (Ch. 2)

Pin dependency versions
  -> pin SDK AND backend/simulator version (Ch. 4)

"Will this fit in budget?"
  -> qubits, depth, AND shot budget, before
     submitting to hardware (Ch. 5)
caption: Classical software engineering still applies — it just needs a quantum-specific adaptation at each step.
